title: Actually: Einstein Misconceptions
description: Famous Einstein “facts” that deserve a second look.

questions.question: Myth: Einstein failed math. Actually, what branch of math had he mastered before age 15?
questions.explanation: When shown a 1935 'Ripley's Believe It or Not' claiming he failed math, Einstein laughed: 'Before I was fifteen I had mastered differential and integral calculus.'

questions.question: Calculus came easy, but his famous dice quote gets garbled. In a 1926 letter he wrote that 'the Old One' does not do what?
questions.explanation: 'I, at any rate, am convinced that He does not throw dice.' It was a jab at quantum randomness—not a statement of religious faith.

questions.question: Einstein's 'does not throw dice' letter went to which physicist friend?
questions.explanation: Born helped build the very quantum theory Einstein was doubting. The two argued about it in letters for decades.

questions.question: Myth: relativity won Einstein his Nobel. Actually, Max Born's friend was honored for explaining what effect?
questions.explanation: Relativity was still too controversial for the committee. The 1921 prize cited 'his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.'

questions.question: Myth: Einstein built the atomic bomb. Actually, years after his photoelectric effect Nobel, he signed a 1939 warning letter to which U.S. president?
questions.explanation: Leo Szilard drafted the letter; Einstein signed it. He never worked on the Manhattan Project and later called signing it 'the one great mistake in my life.'
